iPhone 18 Pro is about to debut, and with this year's major product lineup reshuffle, it will become Apple's new default iPhone like never before.

This year there will be no base iPhone 18, making the iPhone 18 Pro Apple's default new model.

For years, Apple has launched multiple new iPhones every year, and this practice will undoubtedly continue for many more years to come.

However, at this week's Apple event, the iPhone product line will undergo a major restructuring.

Unlike before, Apple will not release two versions — "iPhone" and "iPhone Pro" — this time. The base iPhone 18 will be completely absent.

Multiple sources indicate that Apple will delay the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 until early 2027, meaning the fall lineup will only include the following models:

The release of the iPhone 18 Pro has been pushed back from its original schedule, effectively making it Apple's new default model.

Users looking for an affordable phone can still choose last year's iPhone 17, or the iPhone 17e and iPhone Air. However, regardless of how Apple and its carrier partners promote them this fall and holiday season, there will be no "iPhone 18" as the flagship new model. That role will be taken over by the iPhone 18 Pro.

The iPhone Ultra is priced too high, and its market positioning may be relatively niche by comparison.

Therefore, for the average consumer looking to buy a "new iPhone," Apple will essentially offer only two choices: the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max.

This approach is an interesting experiment that could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling Pro model of the new generation. But with expected price increases, there are also certain risks. With no iPhone 18 available for upgrades in the market, potential buyers may hold on to their current iPhones for longer.

Regardless of the outcome, we will soon find out whether Apple's new strategy is successful.

What do you think of Apple's iPhone lineup changes this year? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
